pr_body:
## Add `IRazorComponentsBuilder.AddWebAssemblyComponents()`

Adds the `IRazorComponentsBuilder.AddWebAssemblyComponents()` extension method. This allows Blazor WebAssembly components to be rendered from a Blazor app that utilizes SSR.

Fixes #46354
pr_comments:
Thanks for the feedback, @SteveSandersonMS! I've added some basic E2E tests to validate interactivity.

I'm re-requesting a review because I've added some new APIs since you last looked (and brought `WebAssembly.Server` into the shared framework).
Hard to see how the CI failure in `Http2WebSocketTests.HEADERS_Received_SecondRequest_ConnectProtocolReset()` could be related - probably flaky.

I can't figure out why `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` is not getting picked up during source build.

@wtgodbe Do you know why this could be happening?

Edit: For context, I added `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to the shared framework and made it a dependency of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Endpoints`. But even though `Components.Endpoints` is getting built in source build, `Components.WebAssembly.Server` is not, causing a compilation error:

```
'IApplicationBuilder' does not contain a definition for 'UseBlazorFrameworkFiles' and no accessible extension method 'UseBlazorFrameworkFiles' accepting a first argument of type 'IApplicationBuilder' could be found (are you missing a using directive or an assembly reference?)
```

(`UseBlazorFrameworkFiles` is defined in `Components.WebAssembly.Server`)

> I can't figure out why `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` is not getting picked up during source build.
> 
> @wtgodbe Do you know why this could be happening?

Some of our custom reference resolution logic is turned off for source build, so it may be referencing an older version of the project. The source build binlog will probably contain useful info about what's getting resolved here. @MichaelSimons is this the kind of situation we've used source build patches for in the past?

> Some of our custom reference resolution logic is turned off for source build, so it may be referencing an older version of the project. The source build binlog will probably contain useful info about what's getting resolved here. 

Taking a cursory look, the WebAssembly components where it looks like UseBlazorFrameworkFiles is defined are excluded from SourceBuild - https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Components/WebAssembly/Directory.Build.props.

> @MichaelSimons is this the kind of situation we've used source build patches for in the past?

No

I've moved `AddWebAssemblyComponents` back to `WebAssembly.Server` because there were some challenges with bringing `WebAssembly.Server` into the shared framework at this time.

@SteveSandersonMS @javiercn Do you think this is good to merge?

issue_context.title: Render a webassembly component into the page
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/46704 describes the general approaches.

The work in this issue covers creating a handler that can be passed in to the HtmlRenderer we plan to provide inside `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web` and registering it in DI to handle webassembly components.

We also need to register the Blazor Webassembly endpoints on to the page inside the ComponentEndpointsDataSource

review_comments:
Without this, the `TestContentPackage` assembly does not get loaded, and [`RootComponentTypeCache`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6575b289081b9f85fb30d01c7b306d1ec5d00a68/src/Components/Shared/src/RootComponentTypeCache.cs#LL24C22-L24C22) can't discover the component.

Would we consider updating `RootComponentTypeCache` to attempt to load an assembly if it couldn't be found?

This is very interesting. Is this just a quirk of the framework that is already the case in .NET 7? For example, if you used `<component ... render-mode="WebAssembly">` (as opposed to declaring the root component in `Program.cs`) could you get the same issue? My guess is yes.

Rather than block your PR on it, I would recommend filing an issue for us to dig into (unless you think you are actively *causing* this issue in your PR here, which doesn't appear to be the case to me).

> Would we consider updating RootComponentTypeCache to attempt to load an assembly if it couldn't be found?

Assuming you mean code that is actually running on WebAssembly (e.g., inside `WebAssemblyHostBuilder`) then yes sure, why not. It's not a security concern in that case.

There could still be a problem since trimming may have removed the component if there was no statically-observable evidence that it was going to be used. However in practice that would be uncommon since we don't trim user assemblies by default. This may change in the future.
We are missing two extension methods `'AddWebAssemblyRenderMode', 'AddServerRenderMode'` to plug a render mode independent of discovery.
Do you think it's fine if I add those as part of this PR?

Looks like those are [already a thing](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/3f389bb07e872cd11b7b7b401ec673465bf89600/src/Components/Endpoints/src/Builder/RazorComponentEndpointConventionBuilder.cs#L47), actually.
